details:
Apps, such as VRCX, that need to access the VRChat API in the users name, require the user to enter their VRChat credentials. This gives the application absolute access to account, not to mention what could happen if the stored credentials get stolen.

Instead, why not allow for developers to register their applications with the VRChat API, so that services or individual devices can be granted scoped permissions. This also has the additional benefit of allowing websites / services to let users login with their VRChat account, directly confirming their VRC identity.

Additionally, as everyone is well aware, many users share their credentials with friends and avatar / world creators so that they can upload content to their account. If the application system with scopes were to be added, the community (or even the VRChat SDK itself) could make a service to allow other users to securely upload / update content to the users account without ever sharing their credentials, and with limitations (such as an expiration date, or limiting access to specific worlds / avatars).
title: Application / Device session support for the API
